eyebrow: California statewide pedestrian safety · US, Bay and SF health
program: Conditional whole-organization value of a $100,000 unrestricted gift

nutshell.headline: Earlier crossing improvements could avert serious injury. Whether an extra gift changes implementation is unknown.
nutshell.body: Central donor estimates are $6.32M per 10 US QALYs, $23.2M Bay and $632M SF. A favorable joint case reaches $29,137 US and $63,737 Bay, but its $1.748M net resource numerator raises US cost to $509,315/10 QALYs.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: California Walks provides donor-supported technical assistance and implementation follow-up. FHWA refuge-island guidance supplies a matching physical safety mechanism.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: Package cost, additional implementation, site injury exposure, displaced health and residence shares are unmeasured priors. A crash reduction is not directly a fatality reduction.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Independently checked conditional research model. No demonstrated marginal package or high-expected-value donation; favorable joint threshold crossing does not establish a recommendation.

summary.label: Central donor cost / 10 QALYs
summary.detail: Same $100,000 unrestricted gift; 0.001583 SF, 0.04317 Bay, 0.1583 US QALYs. All modeled health assumed California residents.

summary.label: Whole gift
summary.detail: 50% to all-in future implementation packages; other portfolio health unquantified and all gift cash retained.

summary.label: Favorable donor / net resource US
summary.detail: Joint favorable scenario, not a confidence bound or calibrated expected value. Bay donor $63,737; SF donor $1.46M.

summary.label: Recipient
summary.detail: Official statewide donation page; EIN corroborated by IRS-derived extract and historical primary grant schedule. No current IRS-status audit.

programSection.body: California Walks combines training, planning, policy work and local organizing. Current pages identify donor-supported no-cost assistance and publicly funded CPBST with implementation follow-up. This model quantifies only hypothetical future support that changes implementation of refuge-island-equivalent crossings.

steps.title: Buy additional support
steps.detail: Half the gift at $25,000 per all-in package buys two nominal packages. Existing agency/foundation support remains baseline.

steps.title: Change implementation
steps.detail: 50% funding additionality and 20% incremental change probability produce 0.2 expected changed projects, conditional on agency and coalition activity.

steps.title: Bring crossings into operation earlier
steps.detail: Six nominal crossings per project and 80% realization produce 0.96 expected target crossings. The alternative loses 0.30 health-equivalent crossings.

steps.title: Count finite net health
steps.detail: Three years of earlier operation after two-year delay; fatal and serious nonfatal events get separate finite tails. Displaced health persists if target implementation fails.

programSection.boundary: Distinct recipient from Walk San Francisco and other road-safety advocates. Never sum their full attribution for the same crossing, funding decision or injured person. Bay includes SF, with separate target and alternative residence shares.

model.headline: Added implementation capacity → finite net crossing safety
model.body: All marginal quantities are judgments. Evidence supports the organizational work and engineering mechanism; it does not identify actual next-gift crossings or QALYs.

equation.label: Whole-gift causal bridge
equation.expression: N = gift × implementation fraction / package cost × funding additionality × incremental project-change probability. Target = N × crossings × realization. Alternative = N × health-equivalent displaced crossings. Regional Q = (target × target residence share − alternative × alternative share) × crash reduction × severity/site transfer × (fatal event rate × finite survival Q + serious nonfatal event rate × finite disability Q) × discounted earlier-operation years − independent harm.
equation.result: Central 2 nominal packages → 0.2 changed projects → 0.96 target versus 0.30 displaced crossing-equivalents → 0.1583 US QALYs.

inputs.label: Implementation allocation / all-in package
inputs.basis: Includes research, engagement and shared operations. No posted package quote; revenue and historic expense ratios do not define the margin.

inputs.label: Funding additionality / incremental project change
inputs.basis: Separate displacement of existing support from contribution conditional on other advocates and agencies. One distinct project per package.

inputs.label: Crossings per project / realized earlier operation
inputs.basis: Operational refuge-island-equivalent sites, not applications or training attendance. No current project queue established.

inputs.label: Displaced health-equivalent crossings per project
inputs.basis: Independent of target realization. May represent another kind of safety investment on the same finite health scale.

inputs.label: Fatal / serious nonfatal events per crossing-year
inputs.basis: Prospective long-run baseline rates, not observed selected-site counts. Fatal and serious nonfatal categories disjoint. Requires matched-site empirical Bayes or controlled exposure analysis to address regression to the mean.

inputs.label: Pedestrian crash reduction / severity-site transfer
inputs.basis: Historical refuge/median guidance for marked crossings. Fatal and serious injury proportionality is unverified; not a CalWalks treatment effect or a claim for every project design.

inputs.label: Earlier-operation years / delay
inputs.basis: 3% discount; no-gift baseline catches up. No current claim that the 2027 ATP application window is open.

inputs.label: Survival utility / mortality / tail
inputs.basis: Central 12.156 QALYs at prevented fatal event. Finite annual survival and discounting; one tail per unique person.

inputs.label: Serious-injury disutility / duration
inputs.basis: Central 1.537 QALYs per nonfatal event after mortality and discounting; assumes persistent average deficit, not validated injury mix. Mortality-only sensitivity retained.

inputs.label: Target Bay/SF and displaced Bay/SF
inputs.range: Favorable 40%/2% versus 20%/2%; zero SF and SF harm
inputs.basis: San Jose activity supports Bay relevance but does not identify resident incidence. All modeled health in California; Bay includes SF.

inputs.label: Target / alternative public and private PV
inputs.basis: Gift-date incremental PV relative to each project's no-gift timing. Includes construction/capital timing and maintenance; transfers and publicly financed private assets excluded.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Joint scenarios are not probability-weighted or confidence intervals. Favorable US/Bay donor prices cross $100,000 per 10 QALYs, while all favorable total-resource prices remain above it. Missing clinical/exposure, causal and cost data prevent high-expected-value inference.
model.fundingBoundary: Official giving supports the statewide organization. Current consulting recognizes foundation/donor support and public CPBST support; neither establishes an unfunded offer. Existing assistance and adopted projects are baseline. Displacement is necessary because ATP is oversubscribed.

reservations: Unverified incremental implementation, target-site exposure, complete project cost and forgone alternatives dominate the result.
Fatal and nonfatal QALY tails are transparent assumptions, not injury-specific clinical estimates.
FY2025 finance values are an IRS-derived extract; raw filing retrieval failed and no functional allocation was independently reconciled.
No complete value estimate for the other half of the unrestricted portfolio.
The highest-value next evidence is a funded-baseline-adjusted queue, site injury history, actual counterfactual schedules and public cost ledger.
